extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and educated readers interested in poetic/epic composition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for composing and judging epic and poetic passages (especially allegory, descriptive episodes, and narrative framing), drawn from commentary on Milton's Paradise Lost. Emphasizes project-introduction, appropriateness of speaker, economy of description, verisimilitude, and sublime imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project introduction in opening book
rubrics_metrics.description: not to omit in the First Book the Project upon which the whole Poem turns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce the poem's central project or purpose early (in the first book) so readers understand the principal design that the entire work will address; the critic notes this was just in Milton's First Book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the proper person to propose the project
rubrics_metrics.description: the Prince of the fallen Angels was the only proper Person to give it Birth, and that the next to him in Dignity was the fittest to second and support it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the character who announces or initiates the central project carefully — it should be someone whose status, temperament, and viewpoint make them naturally suited to conceive or advance that project; mismatching speaker to project weakens plausibility and rhetorical force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prophetic/anticipatory report to elevate subject
rubrics_metrics.description: something wonderfully Beautiful, and very apt to affect the Readers Imagination in this ancient Prophecy or Report in Heaven, concerning the Creation of Man. Nothing could shew more the Dignity of the Species, than this Tradition which ran of them before their Existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ devices like prophecy, report, or pre-existence glimpses to magnify the dignity or importance of characters/events — presenting a subject as spoken of before its existence can deepen its grandeur and affect the reader's imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe grand assemblies in a sublime manner
rubrics_metrics.description: The rising of this great Assembly is described in a very Sublime and Poetical Manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use elevated, sublime diction and striking similes (e.g. 'Their rising all at once was as the Sound Of Thunder heard remote') to convey the scale and majesty of large assemblies or cosmic scenes; such stylistic choices enhance the awe of the moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make diversions and actions suitable to character
rubrics_metrics.description: The Diversions are every way suitable to Beings who had nothing left them but Strength and Knowledge misapplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that incidental activities, entertainments, or diversions reflect the nature, resources, and moral state of the characters (e.g., fallen angels celebrating criminal exploits, contests of arms). Incongruent diversions undermine credibility and thematic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid spinning out circumstances; prefer economy
rubrics_metrics.description: An ordinary Poet would indeed have spun out so many Circumstances to a great Length, and by that means have weakned, instead of illustrated, the principal Fable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of lengthy, exhaustive detailing that distracts from the main plot; concise episodes can illustrate and strengthen the principal fable, while over-elaboration may weaken the narrative's focus and emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concise, striking lines to evoke horror or wonder
rubrics_metrics.description: The monstrous Animals produced in that Infernal World are represented by a single Line, which gives us a more horrid Idea of them, than a much longer Description would have done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes a single powerful line or image conveys horror or sublimity better than extended description; favor concentrated, imagistic phrasing for maximum effect rather than prolix catalogue-like depictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain logical, causal relations in allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: The Genealogy of the several Persons is contrived with great Delicacy. Sin is the Daughter of Satan, and Death the Offspring of Sin. The incestuous Mixture between Sin and Death produces those Monsters and Hell-hounds ... These are the Terrors of an evil Conscience, and the proper Fruits of Sin
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using allegory or personified abstractions, ensure their relationships and origins are coherent and just (e.g., cause-and-effect among symbolic figures), so the allegory conveys a persuasive moral architecture rather than seeming arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress symbolic figures with fitting, vivid attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Figure of Death, [the Regal Crown upon his Head,] his Menace of Satan, his advancing to the Combat, the Outcry at his Birth, are Circumstances too noble to be past over in Silence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equip personified or symbolic figures with concrete, resonant details (regal crown, gestures, threats, birth-outcries) that suit their role and magnify their thematic significance; vivid particulars make abstractions tangible and memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer probability/verisimilitude within imaginative invention
rubrics_metrics.description: I am pleased most with those Passages in this Description which carry in them a greater Measure of Probability, and are such as might possibly have happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance fantastical invention with elements of plausibility; readers often respond best where imaginative scenes contain believable, almost-possible details. Verisimilitude anchors the fantastic and increases reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete physical details to make fantastical voyages plausible
rubrics_metrics.description: Of this kind is his first mounting in the Smoke that rises from the Infernal Pit, his falling into a Cloud of Nitre, and the like combustible Materials, that by their Explosion still hurried him forward in his Voyage; his springing upward like a Pyramid of Fire, with his laborious Passage through that Confusion of Elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ tactile, sensory, and physical specifics (smoke, nitre, explosions, pyramid of fire) to give movement and plausibility to otherwise incredible journeys; such material details create momentum and make the reader accept the extraordinary.
